drafted_from: tool row in tools/benchmark-small-local-models/tool-rows.json, do-work/rank_titles_with_decider.py and test/test_benchmark.py (Decider, Settings)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Rank my two title ideas by how strongly the decider someone/decider-small says yes to: would a viewer click this?"

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own list:settings (see pour), or write your own row record:setting:benchmark-small-local-models~person~<you> whose settings hold {"commands":{"rank_titles_with_decider":{...your defaults}}}.
2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:rank-my-titles-with-a-small-local-model"} and gets its run command.

3. Your AI writes the request as a JSON file (request.json), adds settings_record from your settings row if you keep one, and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/rank_titles_with_decider.py request.json on your computer.
4. It reads the last line the script prints: {"result": ...} or {"error": "what to change"} (exit code 2), then tells you the result in plain words.
5. Show the ranking in order with each p_yes; it is a ranking, not a prediction of clicks. Your own question in the request wins over the settings row's.

worked_examples.title: Two titles ranked by how strongly the decider says yes
worked_examples.ask: Rank my title ideas: would a viewer click this?
worked_examples.given: From tools/benchmark-small-local-models/test/test_benchmark.py (Decider.test_titles_are_ranked_by_yes), run with the test's stand-in decider. titles.json = {"a":"A plain title","b":"Yes, a person on a red screen"}; request.json = {"titles":"titles.json","question":"Would a viewer click this?","model":"someone/decider-small","device":"cpu"}. Run: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/rank_titles_with_decider.py request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"meta":{"model":"someone/decider-small","question":"Would a viewer click this?","load_s":0.0,"ms_per_decision":0,"mps_GB":null,"maxrss_GB":0.01},"ranked":[{"ref":"b","title":"Yes, a person on a red screen","p_yes":0.75},{"ref":"a","title":"A plain title","p_yes":0.5}]}}: title b is first with 0.75, title a second with 0.5.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
